span: Likewise, the practitioners of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi** should also dwell having accomplished laundry-maids and outcaste girls, condensed from the families of delusion and hatred. Regarding "the practitioner who has entered thus," it means one who has exerted effort in the conduct without proliferation. "The nature of **Amitābha**" means the text teaches that whoever meditates on the meditative concentration of **Amitābha** will become like him. Since it is a symbolic illustration, it means that the practitioners of **Akṣobhya** and the others will also become like them. "Will dwell on the ten stages" means becoming the master of the ten stages. "Holding the Lord of Speech" shows the benefits of the **Amitābha** yoga. The Lord of Mind and the Lord of Body should be understood for the yogis of **Akṣobhya** and **Vairocana**; likewise, the Treasury of Space and the Performer of All Activities should be explained for the yogis of **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi**. The text shows this by saying "by possessing that yoga, one becomes like that." "Possessing the supreme lordships" means possessing the lordship of the body and so forth. "All sentient beings" means being distinguished from all sentient beings because one is supreme among one's own and other groups. "Becoming a universal monarch" <term>cakravartin</term> means becoming the master of the circle of the mandala. "Because of being a practitioner of the yoga of conceptualization" means by meditating on the generation stage. After showing the divisions of the <term>mudrās</term> of the generation stage yoga in this way, the text then says "it should also be shown to those who dwell in the completion stage." From the phrase "the four families" down to "it will be achieved before long," it shows that a practitioner of the completion stage should take a girl of any of the families, such as a **Brahmin**, and through the sequence of union, experience the three gnoses—appearance and so forth—arising from causes and conditions. One should dwell focusing on the Vajra Body which is the union of the nature of the unlocalized nirvana arising from the stages of manifest enlightenment of the external and internal self.

Similarly, yogis of the **Ratnasambhava** and **Amoghasiddhi** families should also obtain and abide with laundrymen's and outcaste daughters, condensed from the families of delusion and hatred. Regarding "the practitioner who has thus entered," this refers to one who has exerted effort in the "conduct without elaboration." Regarding "the nature of **Amitābha**," the text shows that whoever meditates on the meditative concentration of **Amitābha** will become like him. This is a figurative illustration; it means that yogis of **Akṣobhya** and the others will also become like them. 

Regarding "will abide on the ten stages," this refers to being the master of the lords of the ten stages. "Holding the Lord of Speech" shows the benefits for a yogi of **Amitābha**. The Lord of the Mind and the Lord of the Body should be understood for the yogis of **Akṣobhya** and **Vairocana** respectively. Similarly, "Space-Treasure" itself and "Performer of All Activities" are explained for the yogis of **Ratna** <note>Ratnasambhava</note> and **Amoghasiddhi**. Furthermore, the text shows that by possessing the yoga of that <note>deity</note>, one becomes like them. 

Regarding "possessing supreme lordship," this means possessing lordship of the body and so forth. "All sentient beings" means being the most excellent among those within one's own group and other groups, thus becoming distinguished from all sentient beings. Regarding "becoming a Universal Monarch" <term>cakravartin</term>, this means becoming the master of the mandala wheel. "Because one is a yogi of conceptualization" means because one meditates on the generation stage.
